neighbours.label: a subject or object pronoun that resumes a just-named person or group right after a conjunction or verb (before he, caused her, ils)
fire: I worked with Daniel for a year before he left for Chicago.
Anna loved the old house, but the move caused her to feel lonely.
We met the Hendersons at church long before they bought the farm.
Tom called his mother as soon as he heard the news.
The coach praised Lisa, although she had missed two games.
My uncle sold the boat after he retired from the navy.
The teachers protested because they had not been paid.
Maria waved at the neighbours while she was waiting for the bus.
quiet: I worked at the bakery for a year before moving to Chicago.
The old house was lovely, but the move felt lonely to everyone.
We visited the church long before the farm was sold.
The phone rang as soon as the news broke on the radio.
The game was close, although two goals were missed.
The boat was sold after the summer season ended.
The protest began because the wages had not been paid.
The bus arrived late while the rain was getting heavier.

notes: card: pronouns/auxiliaries after named entities; probe: 'before she' 0.29, other forms weak. Low confidence.
